notes: Expected retrieval numbers for the synthetic CI fixture (account 9001,
The eval job fails if dense precision@5 or recall@10 drops more than
`tolerance` below these values. Rising numbers never fail the gate.
These are a canary for retrieval breaking, not a quality measurement:
the data behind them is invented. See the header of ci_fixture.yaml.
To update deliberately, when a change legitimately moves the numbers:
run `make eval-fixture`, confirm the new numbers are what the change
should have produced, copy them into `dense` below, and say in the
commit message which change moved them and why the new value is right.
Never update this file to make a red build go green without that.
tolerance_reasoning: Absolute, not relative, and applied to each metric separately.
With 13 pairs, the smallest move either metric can make is one
document changing places in one pair's top-k: 0.2/13 = 0.0154 for
precision@5, and 1/4 relevant ids in the widest pair /13 = 0.0192 for
recall@10. 0.02 therefore absorbs exactly one such move, which is what
a float tie-break on a different CPU could produce, and fails on two,
which no amount of numerical noise explains.
Measured, not guessed: seeding and scoring repeated three times on one
machine, and once more after deleting the database and the Qdrant
collections and re-embedding from the model, produced identical numbers
every time. Against a Qdrant server and against qdrant-client's local
mode, the ranked ids and their order were also identical; only the
cosine scores differed, in the sixth decimal place. The tolerance exists
for the one thing that was not measured, a different runner CPU, and is
set to the smallest value that can survive it.
